title: upgrade: FlashAttentionV2 + fused rotary/rope ops + KV-batching + scheduler tweaks
author: Ava Carter
description:
Context and motivation: Our production traces and the perf-lab benchmarks show that attention is the dominant kernel for many medium-context conversational workloads. This PR upgrades the runtime attention path to use the upstream FlashAttentionV2 kernels where applicable, adds fused-op variants for rotary and RoPE to avoid separate elementwise kernels, and integrates those kernels with the continuous KV-cache batching scheduler. The goal is to reduce per-token latency and GPU utilization while improving throughput for mixed-length workloads.

What this PR does (summary):
- Integrates FlashAttentionV2 (selective fallback to FlashAttnV1 for older GPUs) and exposes a runtime kernel selector based on device capabilities, sequence-length distribution, and model config.
- Adds fused rotary/RoPE operator implementations to be applied inside the attention kernel when the model uses rotary embeddings or RoPE-style position encoding, eliminating an extra elementwise pass.
- Hooks fused kernels into the KV-cache-aware batching scheduler so requests that share prefix caches and compatible seq-len ranges are binned together more aggressively.
- Adds a fast path for small-batch, long-context inference that keeps KV cache pinned and reduces host<->device syncs.
- Adds comprehensive unit and integration tests, microbenchmarks, and perf lab scenarios.

Key design notes:
- Kernel selection: at model load time we probe GPU compute capability and memory; at runtime the scheduler re-evaluates kernel choice every N requests for stability. Fallbacks ensure deterministic outputs even when using fused ops.
- Numerical equivalence: fused-op variants were validated against our reference attention with randomized seed inputs across FP16 and quantized pathways; differences are within numerical noise and identical for deterministic seeds.
- Backward compatibility: older pinned model builds continue to use the legacy attention path until redeployed. We added a runtime flag `REDWOOD_ATTENTION_FORCE_LEGACY` for debugging/rollbacks.

Performance:
- Internal perf lab: 25-40% reduction in p50 token latency on Llama-like models (context 1k-4k) on A100; up to 2.2x throughput improvement for mixed short/long workloads due to batching improvements.
- Cost: expected ~15-30% GPU cost reduction for conversational workloads where attention dominated billing.

Testing and rollout:
- CI: added unit tests and a small e2e perf job.
- Benchmarks: added `bench/attn/flashattnv2_comp.sh` supporting A100 and H100.
- Canary: deploying to Dedicated canary pool with model pin + canary routing for 48h; dashboards added for token latency, KV cache hit rate, and kernel-selection distribution.

Risks and mitigations:
- Regressions in numeric outputs: mitigated with randomized unit tests and a prompt regression suite (included).
- Unexpected GPU driver issues: selective fallback to V1 and per-device gating.
- Scheduler oscillation: we cap kernel re-eval frequency and add smoothing to prevent churn.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel integration and selector
- [x] Fused rotary/RoPE operator implementations
- [x] Scheduler integration and KV-batching adjustments
- [x] Unit tests and perf benchmarks
- [x] Canary dashboards and rollout plan

Related links: Linear ENG-2781 (attention-kernel-upgrade), perf lab ticket ENG-2910, design doc: internal://designs/attn-v2-fused-kernels (internal link).
